verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              यत्तद्वैकर्तनः कर्णो राक्षसश्च घटोत्कचः।  निशीथे समसज्जेतां तद्युद्धमभवत्कथम्॥१॥
कीदृशं चाभवद्रूपं तस्य घोरस्य रक्षसः।  रथश्च कीदृशस्तस्य हयाः सर्वायुधानि च॥२॥
verses.english: What appearance did that terrible Rakshasa then assume? How looked his car and his steeds and what was the nature of his weapons?

verses.sanskrit: किंप्रमाणा हयास्तस्य रथकेतुर्धनुस्तथा।  कीदृशं वर्म चैवास्य शिरस्त्राणं च कीदृशम्॥३॥
verses.english: What was the measure of his horses, his standard and his bow? What kind of armour and head-gear did he then wear? O Sanjaya, expert as you are in the art of narration, tell me all this as I am asking you about them.

verses.sanskrit:
पृष्टस्त्वमेतदाचक्ष्व कुशलो ह्यसि सञ्जय।
              सञ्जय उवाच।
              लोहिताक्षो महाकायस्ताम्रास्यो निम्नितोदरः॥४॥
ऊर्ध्वरोमा हरिश्मश्रुः शंकुकर्णो महाहनुः। आकर्णदारितास्यश्च तीक्ष्णदंष्ट्रः करालवान्॥५॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Ghatotkacha was of gigantic proportion; his eyes were crimson; the hue of his countenance was coppery; his belly was low and sunk. The hair on his body were erect, his head was green; his ears were straight like shafts; and his check bones were high.

verses.sanskrit: सुदीर्घताम्रजिह्वोष्ठो लम्बभ्रूः स्थूलनासिकः।  नीलाङ्गो लोहितग्रीवो गिरिवर्ष्मा भयंकरः॥६॥
verses.english: His mouth was large, extending from ear to ear. His teeth were sharp and four of them were long and pointed. His tongue and his lips were long and of a coppery hue. His brows were long drawn. His nose was thick.

verses.sanskrit: महाकायो यो महाबाहुर्महाशीर्षो महाबलः।  विकृतः परुषस्पर्शो विकचोद्वृद्धपिण्डकः॥७॥
verses.english: His body was of blue complexion, his neck was red. Tall as a mountain he was frightful to look at; of huge stature huge arms and huge head, he possessed unequaled strength.

verses.sanskrit: स्थूलस्फिग्गूढनाभिश्च शिथिलोपचयो महान्।  तथैव हस्ताभरणी महामायोऽङ्गदी तथा॥८॥
verses.english: His limbs were hard and ugly, the hair on his head was tied in a ugly shape upwards. His hips were spacious and his navel was deep. His proportion were gigantic although they were not so strong.
verses.bhavadeepa: विकचश्चासावुद्वृद्धः पिण्डो दृढाङ्गः को मूर्धा यस्य स विकचोद्वृद्धपिण्डकः । पाठान्तरे विकटे विकृते उद्वृद्धे दृढे पिण्डके जङ्घोर्ध्वप्रदेशौ यस्य स विकटोद्वृद्धपिण्डकः ॥७॥

verses.sanskrit: उरसा धारयन्निष्कमग्निमालां यथाऽचलः।  तस्य हेममयं चित्रं बहुरूपाङ्गशोभितम्॥९॥
verses.english: His arms were duly adorned and that one of potent illusive energy wore Angadas and a cuirass on his breast like a circle of fire on the breast of a mountain.
verses.bhavadeepa: स्थूलस्फिकू शिथिलोपचयः स्फिक्प्रदेशे एव शिथिलः श्लथ उपचयो वृद्धिर्यस्य । पाठान्तरे शिखिलः शिखावान् उपचयो ललाटप्रान्तो यस्येत्यर्थः । अङ्गदीतिसाहचर्याद्धस्ताभरणी कटकमुद्रिकादिमान् ॥८॥

verses.sanskrit: तोरणप्रतिमं शुभ्रं किरीटं मूर्ध्न्यशोभत।  कुण्डले बालसूर्याभे मालां हेममयीं शुभाम्॥१०॥
verses.english: A bright and beautiful diadem made of gold adorned his head-diadem of which every part was proportionate and resplendent and which looked like an arch.

verses.sanskrit: धारयन्विपुलं कांस्यं कवचं च महाप्रभम्। किंकिणीशतनिर्घोषं रक्तध्वजपताकिनम्॥११॥
verses.english: His ear-rings were effulgent like the morning sun and his garlands were of gold and exceedingly bright. His body was cased in a massive brazen armour of great effulgence.

verses.sanskrit: ऋक्षचर्मावनद्धाङ्गं नल्वमात्रं महारथम्।  सर्वायुधवरोपेतमास्थितं ध्वजमालिनम्॥१२॥
verses.english: His chariot of gigantic size and of the measure of a Nalva and covered with bear-skin was adorned with a hundred tinkling bells and from its standard fluttered numerous crimson banners.

verses.sanskrit: अष्टचक्रसमायुक्तं मेघगंभीरनिःस्वनम्।  मत्तमातङ्गसंकाशा लोहिताक्षा विभीषणाः॥१३॥
verses.english: It was well furnished with all sorts of weapons, offensive and defensive and was decked with a festoon of bannerets. It possessed eight wheels and its clatter resembled the deep rumble of rain-clouds.

verses.sanskrit: कामवर्णजवा युक्ता बलवन्तः शतं हयाः।  वहन्तो राक्षसं घोरं वालवन्तो जितश्रमाः॥१४॥
verses.english: The horses yoked thereto were stout mettled, of chequered complexion, fleet, of red eyed and like infuriate elephants.

verses.sanskrit: विपुलाभिः सटाभिस्ते ह्रेषमाणा मुहुर्मुहुः।  राक्षसोऽस्य विरूपाक्षः सूतो दीप्तास्यकुंडलः॥१५॥
verses.english: Those indefatigable and spirited steeds bore the dreadful Rakshasa to battle, neighing and throwing back their thick mains repeatedly.

verses.sanskrit: रश्मिभिः सूर्यरश्म्याभैः सञ्जग्राह हयान् रणे।  स तेन सहितस्तस्थावरुणेन यथा रविः॥१६॥
verses.english: A Rakshasa of frightful eyes and decked with bright ear-rings and possessing a fierce mouth acted as his charioteer, checking the horses by the rains that were as bright as the rays of the sun.

verses.sanskrit: संसक्त इव चाभ्रेण यथाऽद्रिर्महता महान्।  दिवःस्पृक् सुमहान्केतुः स्यन्दनेऽस्य समुच्छ्रितः॥१७॥
verses.english: Accompanied by that charioteer he came like the sun accompanied by his charioteer Arjuna (dawn). Looking like a high mountain enveloped in cloudy masses.

verses.sanskrit: रक्तोत्तमाङ्गः क्रव्यादो गृध्रः परमभभीषणः।  वासवाशनिनिर्घोषं दृढज्यमतिविक्षिपन्॥१८॥
verses.english: A huge standard, touching the very clouds was set upon his chariot. A dreadful vulture of crimson body and flash-eating was the device on his standards.

verses.sanskrit: व्यक्तं किष्कुपरीणाहं द्वादशारत्निकार्मुकम्।  रथाक्षमात्रैरिषुभिः सर्वाः प्रच्छादयन्दिशः॥१९॥
verses.english: The Rakshasa then advanced, forcibly stretching his bow of which the twang resembled the rattle of Indra's thunder and the string was very though and which measured twelve Aranis in length and one in breadth

verses.sanskrit: तस्यां वीरापहारिण्यां निशायां कर्णमभ्ययात्। तस्य विक्षिपतश्चापं रथे विष्टभ्य तिष्ठतः॥२०॥
verses.english: Filling all the quarters of the heaven with arrows of the measures of the Aksha of a car, the Rakshasa assailed Karna in that night that witnessed the destruction of so many heroes.
verses.bhavadeepa: किष्कुर्हस्तस्तन्मितः परीणाहो विस्तारो यस्य अरत्निर्निरष्टमांशः करः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: अश्रूयत धनुर्घोषो विस्फूर्जितमिवाशनेः।  तेन वित्रास्यमानानि तव सैन्यानि भारत॥२१॥
verses.english: Proudly seated on his car, as he stretched his bow, the twang that was heard resembled the rumble of the roaring thunder.

verses.sanskrit: समकम्पन्त सर्वाणि सिन्धोरिव महोर्मयः।  तमापतन्तं संप्रेक्ष्य विरूपाक्षं विभीषणम्॥२२॥
verses.english: Frightened at that sound, your troops O Bharata, trembled like the surging billows of the sea.

verses.sanskrit: उत्स्मयन्निव राधेयस्त्वरमाणोऽभ्यवारयत्।  ततः कर्णोऽभ्ययादेनमस्यन्नस्यन्तमन्तिकात्॥२३॥
verses.english: Beholding that one of frightful eyes and dreadful aspect rush towards himself, the son of Radha quickly withstood him in all cheerfulness.

verses.sanskrit: मातङ्ग इव मातङ्गं यूथर्षभमिवर्षभः।  स सन्निपातस्तुमुलस्तयोरासीद्विशांपते॥२४॥
verses.english: Karna then advanced against the smiting Rakshasa smiting him in return from a near point, like an elephant rushing against another or a bull charging another.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णराक्षसयो राजन्निन्द्रशम्बरयोरिव।  तौ प्रगृह्य महावेगे धनुषी भीमनिःस्वने॥२५॥
verses.english: Then the dreadful collision, o mighty monarch, that took place between Karna and the Rakshasa, resembled ( ruler of men that between Shakra and Samvara (in days gone by).

verses.sanskrit: प्राच्छादयेतामन्योन्यं तक्षमाणौ महेषुभिः।  ततः पूर्णायतोत्सृष्टैरिषुभिर्नतपर्वभिः॥२६॥
verses.english: Each then grasping a fearful bow of loud twang began to wound and cover the other with mighty shafts.

verses.sanskrit: न्यवारयेतामन्योन्यं कांस्ये निर्भिद्य वर्मणी।  तौ नखैरिव शार्दूलौ दन्तैरिव महाद्विपौ॥२७॥
रथशक्तिभिरन्योन्यं विशिखैश्च ततक्षतुः।  सञ्छिन्दन्तौ च गात्राणि सन्दधानौ च सायकान्॥२८॥
verses.english: Then like two tigers mangling each other with claws or two elephants with their tusks, they mangled each other with their lances and arrows and javelins.

verses.sanskrit: दहन्तौ च शरोल्काभिर्दुष्प्रेक्ष्यौ च बभूवतुः।  तौ तु विक्षतसर्वाङ्गौ रुधिरौघपरिप्लुतौ॥२९॥
verses.english: Mangling each other's body, aiming their shafts at each other and burning each other with myriads of shafts, they could not be gazed at.
verses.bhavadeepa: रथशक्तिभिः रथाक्षमात्रैरिति प्रागुक्तैः, रथाक्षतुल्यैरित्यर्थः । ‘रथः स्यन्दनदेहयोः’ इति कोशाद्देहानुकूलशक्तिमद्भिरिति वा ॥२८॥

verses.sanskrit: विभ्राजेतां यथा वारि स्रवन्तौ गैरिकाचलौ।  तौ शराग्रविनुन्नाङ्गौ निर्भिन्दन्तौ परस्परम्॥३०॥
verses.english: Covered with arrow-wounds all over the body and steeped in torrents of blood, they both looked beautiful like two hills of red chalk with rivulets flowing down their sides.

verses.sanskrit: नाकम्पयेतामन्योन्यं यतमानौ महाद्युती। तत्प्रवृत्तं निशायुद्धं चिरं सममिवाभवत्॥३१॥
verses.english: Those two mighty car-warriors, though they were striving hard and each had his limbs torn open with points of shafts, could not make each other flinch or tremble.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणयोर्दीव्यतो राजन्कर्णराक्षसयोर्मृधे।  तस्य सन्दधतस्तीक्ष्णाञ्छरांश्चासक्तमस्यतः॥३२॥
verses.english: That nocturnal combat between Karna and the Rakshasa, with both regarded as a game having their lives for the stake, seemed for a long time to be a equal one.

verses.sanskrit: धनुर्घोषेण वित्रस्ताः स्वे परे च तदाऽभवन्।  घटोत्कचं यदा कर्णो विशेषयति नो नृप॥३३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: तस्य घटोत्कचस्य आसक्तमन्योन्यसंसक्तं यथा स्यात्तथा शरानस्यतः । आशक्तमिति पाठे यावच्छक्ति आर्षोऽच्प्रत्ययः समासान्तः ॥३२॥

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रादुष्करोद्दिव्यमस्त्रमस्त्रविदां वरः।  कर्णेन संधितं दृष्ट्वा दिव्यमस्त्रं घटोत्कचः॥३४॥
verses.english: Then, O king, Karna was unable to gain any advantage over Ghatotkacha. Thereafter that foremost of all persons versed in the use of weapons, invoked into existence a celestial weapon.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुश्चक्रे महामायां राक्षसीं पाण्डुनन्दनः।  शूलमुद्गरधारिण्या शैलपादपहस्तया॥३५॥
verses.english: Thereupon the king of the Rakshasas beholding a celestial weapon aimed at him, by Karna, brought into use his Rakshasa illusion.

verses.sanskrit: रक्षसां घोररूपाणां महत्या सेनया वृतः।  तमुद्यतमहाचापं दृष्ट्वा ते व्यथिता नृपाः॥३६॥
verses.english: Beholding the Rakshasa come with an uplifted weapon like the Destroyer of beings armed with his fatal bludgeon, all the kings of your host were filled with terror.

verses.sanskrit: भूतान्तकमिवायान्तं कालदण्डोग्रधारिणम्।  घटोत्कचप्रयुक्तेन सिंहनादेन भीषिताः॥३७॥
प्रसुस्रुवुर्गजा मूत्रं विव्यधुश्च नरा भृशम्।  ततोऽश्मवृष्टिरत्युग्रा महत्यासीत्समन्ततः॥३८॥
अर्धरात्रेऽधिकबलैर्विमुक्ता रक्षसां बलैः।  आयसानि च चक्राणि भुशुण्ड्यः शक्तितोमराः॥३९॥
verses.english: Then a mighty shower of rocks and stones fell on all sides, being poured incessantly by the Rakshasas, who had acquired greater strength, in consequence of the hour being mid-night.

verses.sanskrit: पतन्त्यविरलाःशूलाः शतघ्न्यः पट्टिशास्तथा।  तदुग्रमतिरौद्रं च दृष्ट्वा युद्धं नराधिप॥४०॥
verses.english: Seeing that furious and terrible battle the kings, your sons and Karna too, being (greatly) distressed, ran away from the battle field).

verses.sanskrit: पुत्राश्च तव योधाश्च व्यथिता विप्रदुद्रुवुः।  तत्रैकोऽस्त्रबलश्लाघी कर्णो मानी न विव्यथे॥४१॥
verses.english: Then beholding that battle fierce to the extreme, your son and your warriors sorely afflicted (with terror) took to their heels.

verses.sanskrit: व्यधमच्च शरैर्मायां तां घटोत्कचनिर्मिताम्।  मायायां तु प्रहीणायाममर्षाच्च घटोत्कचः॥४२॥
verses.english: The proud Karna alone, ever boastful of strength of his weapons, was not terrified and he continued to stay on the field, baffling with his arrows the illusions displayed by Ghatotkacha. Ghatotkacha then discharged dreadful arrows for compassing the death of Suta's son.

verses.sanskrit: विससर्ज शरान् घोरान्सूतपुत्रं त आविशन्।  ततस्ते रुधिराभ्यक्ता भित्त्वा कर्णं महाहवे॥४३॥
विविशुर्धरणीं बाणाः संक्रुद्धा इव पन्नगाः।  सूतपुत्रस्तु संक्रुद्धो लघुहस्तः प्रतापवान्॥४४॥
verses.english: And then speedily entered into the earth like serpents (entering) an ant-hill. The lighthanded and powerful Ashvatthama too, excited with wrath.

verses.sanskrit: घटोत्कचमतिक्रम्य बिभेद दशभिः शरैः।  घटोत्कचो विनिर्भिन्नः सूतपुत्रेण मर्मसु॥४५॥
verses.english: Furiously pierced Ghatotkacha with ten arrows. Deeply pierced in the vital parts by the son of Drona, Ghatotkacha.

verses.sanskrit: चक्रं दिव्यं सहस्त्रारमगृह्णाद्व्यथितो भृशम्।  क्षुरान्तं बालसूर्याभं मणिरत्नविभूषितम्॥४६॥
verses.english: Pierced in his vital parts and extremely pained by the son of Suta, Ghatotkacha took up a discus of celestial make having a thousands pokes.

verses.sanskrit: चिक्षेपाधिरथेः क्रुद्धो भैमसेनिर्जिघांसया।  प्रविद्धमतिवेगेन विक्षिप्तं कर्णसायकैः॥४७॥
verses.english: Then the son of Bhima, desirous of slaying the son of Adhiratha, hurled at the latter that discus furnished with a razor-sharp edge, of the effulgence of the morning sun and decked with gems and jewels.

verses.sanskrit: अभाग्यस्येव संकल्पस्तन्मोघमपतद्भुवि। घटोत्कचस्तु संक्रुद्धो दृष्ट्वा चक्रं निपातितम्॥४८॥
कर्णं प्राच्छादयद्बाणैः स्वर्भानुरिव भास्करम्।  सूतपुत्रस्त्वसंभ्रान्तो रुद्रोपेन्द्रेन्द्रविक्रमः॥४९॥
verses.english: Beholding his discus thus baffled, Ghatotkacha was highly enraged and he then covered Karna with his arrows like Rahu covering the sun.

verses.sanskrit: घटोत्कचरथं तूर्णं छादयामास पत्रिभिः।  घटोत्कचेन क्रुद्धेन गदा हेमाङ्गदा तदा॥५०॥
verses.english: But the son of Suta Karna possessed prowess equal to that of Rudra or Upendra or Indra himself dauntlessly covered Ghatotkacha's chariot with his winged arrows.

verses.sanskrit: क्षिप्ता भ्राम्य शरैः साऽपि कर्णेनाभ्याहताऽपतत्।  ततोऽन्तरिक्षमुत्पत्य कालमेघ इवोन्नदन्॥५१॥
verses.english: Thereafter a gold-decked mace was whirled and hurled at Karna by Ghatotkacha. But the former cutting it off with his arrows felled it on the ground.

verses.sanskrit: प्रववर्ष महाकायो द्रुमवर्षं नभस्तलात्।  ततो मायाविनं कर्णो भीमसेनसुतं दिवि॥५२॥
verses.english: Then soaring into the sky and roaring like destructive clouds, the huge-bodied Rakshasa poured a veritable shower of trees from the skies.

verses.sanskrit: मार्गणैरभिविव्याध घनं सूर्य इवांशुभिः।  तस्य सर्वान्हयान् हत्वा संछिद्य शतधा रथम्॥५३॥
verses.english: And whirling it, (he) hurled (that mace at Ashvatthama). But the son of Drona, striking it (with arrows) filled it (to the ground). Then, leaping up in the air and roaring like black clouds, Anjaniparva began to pour down son showers of trees from the firmament. Then the son of Drona began to pierce that one capable of (creating) illusions by means of shafts in the sky as the sun (pierces) the clouds with his rays. Seated on his car again decked with gold, when that one of great strength.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्यवर्षच्छरैः कर्णः पर्जन्य इव वृष्टिमान्।  न चास्यासीदनिर्भिन्नं गात्रे द्व्यङ्गुलमन्तरम्॥५४॥
verses.english: Next cutting his car into fragments and slaying all his horses, Karna covered him with arrows, like a cloud charged with rain.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽदृश्यत मुहूर्तेन श्वाविच्छललितो यथा।  न हयान्न रथं तस्य न ध्वजं न घटोत्कचम्॥५५॥
verses.english: There was not even space of two finger's breadth in the body of Ghatotkacha that was not pierced with Karna's shafts. Soon the Rakshasa appeared to be like a porcupine with its quills erect.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्टवन्तः स्म समरे शरौघैरभिसंवृतम्।  स तु कर्णस्य तद्दिव्यमस्त्रमस्त्रेण शातयन्॥५६॥
verses.english: So completely was he covered with shafts that we could not in that battle, any longer see either Ghatotkacha's person or his horses or his car or standard.

verses.sanskrit: मायायुद्धेन मायावी सूतपुत्रमयोधयत्।  सोऽयोधयत्तदा कर्णं मायया लाघवेन च॥५७॥
verses.english: Then the Rakshasa versed in illusion destroying by his own weapon the celestial weapon of Karna, began to fight with Suta's son, aided by his own illusive powers.

verses.sanskrit: अलक्ष्यमाणानि दिवि शरजालानि चापतन्।  भैमसेनिर्महामायो मायया कुरुसत्तम॥५८॥
verses.english: Indeed he fought on with Karna, aided by his illusive powers and exhibiting his great agility. Then showers of shafts began to fall from invisible quarters in the skies.

verses.sanskrit: विचचार महाकायो मोहयन्निव भारत।  स तु कृत्वा विरूपाणि वदनान्यशुभानि च॥५९॥
verses.english: Then Bhimasena's son possessed of potent powers of illusion, O best of the Kurus, assumed, by the help of those powers, a dreadful appearance and began to confound the Kouravas, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: अग्रसत्सूतपुत्रस्य दिव्यान्यस्त्राणि मायया।  पुनश्चापि महाकायः संछिन्नः शतधा रणे॥६०॥
verses.english: The puissant Rakshasa then assuming many terrible heads, began to swallow up the celestial weapons of Karna.

verses.sanskrit: गतसत्त्वो निरुत्साहः पतितः खाद्ध्यदृश्यत।  तं हतं मन्यमानाः स्म प्राणदन्कुरुपुङ्गवाः॥६१॥
verses.english: Soon again, the huge Rakshasas with hundred of wounds on his body seemed to lie cheerlessly and like one dead, on the field.

verses.sanskrit: अथ देहैर्नवैरन्यैर्दिक्षु सर्वास्वदृश्यत।  पुनश्चापि महाकायः शतशीर्षः शतोदर॥६२॥
व्यदृश्यत महाबाहुर्मैनाक इव पर्वतः।  अङ्गुष्ठमात्रो भूत्वा च पुनरेव स राक्षसः॥६३॥
सागरोर्मिरिवोद्धूतस्तिर्यगूर्ध्वमवर्तत।  वसुधां दारयित्वा च पुनरप्सु न्यमज्जत॥६४॥
verses.english: Once again he became small about the transversely or soared high like the surging billows of the ocean.

verses.sanskrit: अदृश्यत तदा तत्र पुनरुन्मज्जितोऽन्यतः।  सोऽवतीर्य पुनस्तस्थौ रथे हेमपरिष्कृते॥६५॥
verses.english: Tearing through the earth, he dived again into the waters. Once seen here he was next seen rising on the surface at a different place.

verses.sanskrit: क्षितिं खं च दिशश्चैव माययाऽभ्येत्य दंशितः।  गत्वा कर्णरथाभ्याशं व्यचरत्कुण्डलाननः॥६६॥
verses.english: Then coming down from the welkin, he was seen standing, covered in mail, on a chariot adorned with gold, having wandered through earth and sky and all the points of the compass aided by his powers of illusion.

verses.sanskrit: प्राह वाक्यमसंभ्रान्तः सूतपुत्रं विशांपते। तिष्ठेदानीं क्व मे जीवन्सूतपुत्र गमिष्यसि॥६७॥
verses.english: Then going near the vicinity of Karna's chariot, Ghatotkacha with his his ear-rings moving, dauntlessly addressed the son of Suta, O king, in these words.

verses.sanskrit: युद्धश्रद्धामहं तेऽद्य विनेष्यामि रणाजिरे।  इत्युक्त्वा रोषताम्राक्षं रक्षः क्रूरपराक्रमम्॥६८॥
उत्पपातान्तरिक्षं च जहास च सुविस्तरम्।  कर्णमभ्यहनच्चैव गजेन्द्रमिव केसरी॥६९॥
verses.english: Having thus spoken, the Rakshasa of fierce prowess, with his eyes red in rage, soared into the sky and laughed a tremendous laugh.

verses.sanskrit: रथाक्षमात्रैरिषुभिरभ्यवर्षद्धटोत्कचः।  रथिनामृषभं कर्णं धाराभिरिव तोयदः॥७०॥
शरवृष्टिं च तां कर्णो दूरात्प्राप्तामशातयत्।  दृष्ट्वा च विहतां मायां कर्णेन भरतर्षभ॥७१॥
verses.english: That foremost car-warrior viz., Karna, like a could with showers of rain. But Karna repulsed that arrowy shower before it could reach him.

verses.sanskrit: घटोत्कचस्ततो मायां ससर्जान्तर्हितः पुनः।  सोऽभवद्गिरिरत्युच्चः शिखरैस्तरुसंकटैः॥७२॥
verses.english: Ghatotkacha then disappeared from view again and created (another) illusion (by virtue of this new illusion); he assumed the shape of a towering mountain abounding with peaks and trees.

verses.sanskrit: शूलप्रासासिमुसलजलप्रस्रवणो महान्। तमञ्जनचयप्रख्यं कर्णो दृष्ट्वा महीधरम्॥७३॥
verses.english: And having a great fountain of water from which spears, lances, swords and heavy clubs, flowed incessantly. The son of Drona, beholding that mountain looking like a mass of antimony.

verses.sanskrit: प्रपातैरायुधान्युग्राण्युद्वहन्तं न चुक्षुभे।  स्मयन्निव ततः कर्णो दिव्यमस्त्रमुदैरयत्॥७४॥
verses.english: Beholding that mountain resembling a heap of antimony from which fierce weapons continuously flowed out, Karna was not at all daunted.

verses.sanskrit: ततः सोऽस्त्रेण शैलेन्द्रो विक्षिप्तो वै व्यनश्यत।  ततः स तोयदो भूत्वा नीलः सेन्द्रायुधो दिवि॥७५॥
verses.english: By means of that weapon he soon destroyed that prince of mountains. Then he (i.e., Ghatotkacha) wearing the shape of a blue cloud adorned with rain-bow in the firmament.

verses.sanskrit: अश्मवृष्टिभिरत्युग्रः सूतपुत्रमवाकिरत्।  अथ सन्धाय वायव्यमस्त्रमस्त्रविदां वरः॥७६॥
verses.english: Thereafter the Rakshasa becoming a blue cloud decked with the rain-bow began to cover the son of Suta with a fierce shower of stones.

verses.sanskrit: व्यधमत्कालमेघं तं कर्णो वैकर्तनो वृषः।  स मार्गणगणैः कर्णो दिशः प्रच्छाद्य सर्वशः॥७७॥
verses.english: The son Drona destroyed that rising blue cloud covering all points completely with numerous arrows, the son of Drona.

verses.sanskrit: जघानास्त्रं महाराज घटोत्कचसमीरितम्।  ततः प्रहस्य समरे भैमसेनिर्महाबलः॥७८॥
verses.english: Then, O king, covered the quarters of the compass with his arrows, Karna baffled the weapons shot by Ghatotkacha.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुश्चक्रे महामायां कर्णं प्रति महारथम्।  स दृष्ट्वा पुनरायान्तं रथेन रथिनां वरम्॥७९॥
verses.english: Then the highly puissant son of Bhimasena smiling the while invoked into existence an allpowerful illusion against that mighty carwarrior viz., Karna.

verses.sanskrit: घटोत्कचमसंभ्रान्तं राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्।  सिंहशार्दूलसदृशैर्मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमैः॥८०॥
verses.english: That foremost of two-legged creatures. destroyed one hundred thousand cars. He (then) saw Ghatotkach come again fearlessly on a car bending his bow and surrounded by a host of Rakshasas, resembling (in shape) lions and tigers, endued with the prowess of infuriated elephants.

verses.sanskrit: गजस्थैश्च रथस्थैश्च वाजिपृष्ठगतैस्तथा।  नानाशस्त्रधरैर्घोरैर्नानाकवचभूषणैः॥८१॥
verses.english: Riding on elephants, cars and horses and possessed of unnatural, faces head and necks. Those followers of the son of Hidimva.

verses.sanskrit: वृतं घटोत्कचं क्रूरैर्मरुद्भिरिव वासवम्।  दृष्ट्वा कर्णो महेष्वासो योधयामास राक्षसम्॥८२॥
घटोत्कचस्ततः कर्णं विद्ध्वा पञ्चभिराशुगैः।  ननाद भैरवं नादं भीषयन्सर्वपार्थिवान्॥८३॥
भूयश्चाञ्जलिकेनाथ स मार्गणगणं महत्।  कर्णहस्तस्थितं चापं चिच्छेदाशु घटोत्कचः॥८४॥
अथान्यद्धनुरादाय दृढं भारसहं महत्।  विचकर्ष बलात्कर्ण इन्द्रायुधमिवोच्छ्रितम्॥८५॥
verses.english: some

verses.sanskrit: ततः कर्णो महाराज प्रेषयामास सायकान्।  सुवर्णपुङ्खाञ्छत्रुघ्नान् खेचरान् राक्षसान्प्रति॥८६॥
verses.english: Uttered a tremendous war-cry, filling all the kings with terror. Once more with an Anjalika, Ghatotkacha quickly cut-off the bow of Karna held in his hands together with the arrows fitted thereon. Thereupon Karna taking up another mighty bow capable of bearing a greater strain and looking like the bow of Indra itself, began to stretch it forcibly; thereafter, O king, Karna sped arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तद्बाणैरर्दितं यूथं रक्षसां पीनवक्षसाम्।  सिंहेनेवार्दितं वन्यं गजानामाकुलं कुलम्॥८७॥
विधम्य राक्षसान्बाणैः साश्वसूतगजान्विभुः।  ददाह भगवान्वह्निर्भूतानीव युगक्षये॥८८॥
स हत्वा राक्षसीं सेनां शुशुभे सूतनन्दनः।  पुरेव त्रिपुरं दग्ध्वा दिवि देवो महेश्वरः॥८९॥
तेषु राजसहस्त्रेषु पाण्डवेयेषु मारिष। नैनं निरीक्षितुमपि कश्चिच्छक्नोति पार्थिवः॥९०॥
ऋते घटोत्कचाद्राजन् राक्षसेन्द्रान्महाबलात्। भीमवीर्यबलोपेतात् क्रुद्धाद्वैवस्वतादिव॥९१॥
verses.english: There was none who could then even look at Karna. O ruler of men, except the powerful Ghatotkacha, that foremost of Rakshasas who was possessed of terrible energy and mighty and who burning with wrath, then looked like the himself. Excited as he was with wrath flames of fire seemed to issue out of his eyes, like burning drops of oil from a pair of flambeaus; then striking his palms against each other and biting his nether lip.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य क्रुद्धस्य नेत्राभ्यां पावकः समजायत।  महोल्काभ्यां यथा राजन् सार्चिषः स्नेहबिन्दवः॥९२॥
तलं तलेन संहत्य सन्दश्य दशनच्छदम्। रथमास्थाय च पुनर्मायया निर्मितं तदा॥९३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: उल्काभ्यां सर्जरसमिश्रोमुल्काभ्यां ततो हि दीप्तस्य सर्जरसस्य कणाः सस्नेहत्वात्सार्चिष एव पतन्तीति प्रसिद्धम् ॥९२॥

verses.sanskrit: युक्तं गजनिभैर्वाहैः पिशाचवदनैः खरैः। स सूतमब्रवीत्क्रुद्धः सूतपुत्राय मां वह॥९४॥
स ययौ घोररूपेण रथेन रथिनां वरः। द्वैरथं सूतपुत्रेण पुनरेव विशांपते॥९५॥
स चिक्षेप पुनः क्रुद्धः सूतपुत्राय राक्षसः।  अष्टचक्रां महाघोरामशनिं रुद्रनिर्मिताम्॥९६॥
द्वियोजनसमुत्सेधां योजनायामविस्तराम्।  आयसीं निचितां शूलैः कदम्बमिव केसरैः॥९७॥
verses.english: An Asani of dreadful appearance furnished with eight wheels and manufactured by Rudra himself. Placing his bow on his car and jumping down on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: तामवप्लुत्य जग्राह कर्णो न्यस्य महद्धनुः।  चिक्षेप चैनां तस्यैव स्यन्दनात्सोऽवपुप्लुवे॥९८॥
साश्वसूतध्वजं यानं भस्म कृत्वा महाप्रभा।  विवेश वसुधां भित्त्वा सुरास्तत्र विसिस्मियुः॥९९॥
verses.english: That dreadful Asani of great luster having consumed to ashes the car together with the steeds, the driver and the standard, rived the earth and (then) penetrated into it.

verses.sanskrit: कर्णं तु सर्वभूतानि पूजयामासुरञ्जसा। यदवप्लुत्य जग्राह देवसृष्टां महाशनिम्॥१००॥
एवं कृत्वा रणे कर्ण आरुरोह रथं पुनः। ततो मुमोच नाराचान्सूतपुत्रः परन्तप॥१०१॥
verses.english: Inasmuch as he succeeded in grasping the Asani of celestial make, having jumped down from his car. Having achieved this feat, Karna again ascended his car.

verses.sanskrit: अशक्यं कर्तुमन्येन सर्वभूतेषु मानद। यदकार्षीत्तदा कर्णः संग्रामे भीमदर्शने॥१०२॥
स हन्यमानो नाराचैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतः।  गन्धर्वनगराकारः पुनरन्तरधीयत॥१०३॥
verses.english: Thereafter that afflicter of foes, namely the son of Suta began to shoot his arrows. O giver of honour what Karna then achieved in that battle of fierce aspect was incapable of being achieved by any other creatures. Then struck with his Narachas like a mountain by showers of rain.

verses.sanskrit: एवं स वै महाकायो मायया लाघवेन च।  अस्त्राणि तानि दिव्यानि जघान रिपुसूदनः॥१०४॥
निहन्यमानेष्वस्त्रेषु मायया तेन रक्षसा।  असंभ्रान्तस्तदा कर्णस्तद्रक्षः प्रत्ययुध्यत॥१०५॥
verses.english: Ghatotkacha of aerial from once more disappeared from the view. Fighting in this way, the huge Rakshasa, the slayer of foes, destroyed the celestial weapons of Karna, by means of high agility and illusive powers. Thus although his weapons were destroyed by the illusive powers of that Rakshasa.

verses.sanskrit: ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज भैमसेनिर्महाबलः। चकार बहुधाऽऽत्मानं भीषयाणो महारथान्॥१०६॥
ततो दिग्भ्यः समापेतुः सिंहव्याघ्रतरक्षवः।  अग्निजिह्वाश्च भुजगा विहगाश्चाप्ययोमुखाः॥१०७॥
verses.english: Multiplied himself many times thereby inspiring terror in to the hearts of mighty carwarriors. Thereafter from all the points of the compass lions, tigers, hyenas, fire-tongued snakes and iron-beaked rangers of the sky, began to issue out. Covered with the swiftlyflying arrows shot from Karna's bow.

verses.sanskrit: स कीर्यमाणो विशिखैः कर्णचापच्युतैः शरैः।  नागराडिव दुष्प्रेक्ष्यस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत॥१०८॥
राक्षसाश्च पिशाचाश्च यातुधानास्तथैव च।  शालावृकाश्च बहवो वृकाश्च विकृताननाः॥१०९॥
ते कर्णं क्षपयिष्यन्तः सर्वतः समुपाद्रवन्।  अथैनं वाग्भिरुग्राभिस्त्रासयांचक्रिरे तदा॥११०॥
उद्यतैर्बहुभिर्घोरैरायुधैः शोणितोक्षितैः।  तेषामनेकैरेकैकं कर्णो विव्याध सायकैः॥१११॥
प्रतिहत्य तु तां मायां दिव्येनास्त्रेण राक्षसीम्।  आजघान हयानस्य शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः॥११२॥
ते भग्ना विक्षताङ्गाश्च भिन्नपृष्ठाश्च सायकैः।  वसुधामन्वपद्यन्त पश्यतस्तस्य रक्षसः॥११३॥
स भग्नमायो हैडिम्बिः कर्णं वैकर्तनं तदा।  एष ते विदधे मृत्युमित्युक्त्वाऽन्तरधीयत॥११४॥
verses.english: Fell down on the earth, even before the eyes of that Rakshasa. The son of Hidimba seeing his illusions baffled once more made himself invincible, speaking thus to Vikartana's son-"I will presently compass your slaughter."
